headline: Any agent, any model, a chat on the right like Claude Code, and faster long threads
pill: any agent and model, chat in the right sidebar, threads list
summary: Turnhuddle 0.3 is rebuilt on what we learned from Claude Code and T3 Code. The chat moves to VS Code's right-hand sidebar with a single header, every thread is listed on the left, each seat can be Claude Code, Codex or (in preview) Gemini with any model, and each agent keeps its own session for the whole thread, so replies don't resend the conversation.

highlights.title: Chat on the right, threads on the left
highlights.text: Like Claude Code, the chat is one **Turnhuddle** panel in VS Code's right-hand sidebar (VS Code 1.106 or later; older versions keep it in the activity bar). **Threads** in the activity bar lists every conversation: bookmarked first, running ones on top, with state and age, and Bookmark and Archive on each row. The leftover *Conversations* section from 0.2 is gone. Use the Turnhuddle button in the editor title bar, or **Turnhuddle: Open Chat**, to bring the chat forward.
highlights.alt: VS Code with the Threads list on the left and the Turnhuddle chat in the right-hand sidebar, where Claude Opus 5.5 and Codex GPT-6.2-Sol agree on a plan

highlights.title: Choose the agent and model for each seat
highlights.text: The two names under the message box are the seats. Click one for a picker like Claude Code's: every provider, the models found on your machine (the Codex models your account offers, Claude's aliases and the models you've used recently, Gemini's), **Other model…** for any id, and **Swap drafter and reviewer**. Seat the same provider twice with two models if you like. The choice applies to the open conversation and to new ones.
highlights.alt: The agent picker for the reviewer seat, listing Claude, Codex and Gemini models with the current choice checked, and Swap drafter and reviewer at the end

improvements: **Faster long threads.** Each seat keeps its own Claude Code or Codex session for the whole thread (`claude --resume`, `codex exec resume`), so later turns send only what's new instead of the whole conversation. In our tests a reply round took about 30 s, against about 50 s before. Turn this off with `turnhuddle.keepAgentSessions`.

**Gemini CLI (preview).** Seat Gemini in either role once the `gemini` CLI is installed and signed in. It's built against the CLI's documented streaming output and tested with recorded output; please report how it works for you.
Built for more providers: each one is a single entry in a registry, so adding the next CLI doesn't touch the chat, history or prompts.
The composer is calmer: the seats, the mode and Send. The round status appears while a round runs, and each seat's tooltip shows its model and effort; **Effort and other settings…** is in the picker.

New commands: **Choose the Drafter's Agent and Model**, **Choose the Reviewer's Agent and Model** and **Swap Drafter and Reviewer**. New settings: `turnhuddle.drafter`, `turnhuddle.reviewer` and `turnhuddle.geminiPath`.
**Check CLI Installations** lists every provider, marking the ones you don't use as optional.
Sessions Turnhuddle starts for its agents no longer show up in **Continue from a Claude Code or Codex session**.
fixes: Conversations from earlier versions open unchanged: Claude's messages are the drafter's and Codex's the reviewer's.
